loop.top3_why: The series is strongly trend‑dominated and exhibits high predictability. In such cases a simple mean of the full model pool tends to capture the dominant trend component while still averaging out model‑specific noise. The mean strategy shows the best overall validation score (0.6424) and its per‑window performance is consistently close to the best, indicating stability across the three windows. Given the unstable model ranking and the risk of correlated errors, a robust yet straightforward mean is preferable to more complex or potentially over‑fitting methods such as DBA or median, which do not provide a clear advantage here.
loop.top3_why_not: B (DBA) achieves the same validation score but relies on DTW barycentering, which can over‑fit to the limited three validation windows and may be sensitive to the non‑stationary trend. C (median) is robust to outliers, but its per‑window scores are lower in the first two windows and only slightly better in the third, offering no net benefit over the mean while potentially discarding useful information from well‑performing models.
